answer: New agents enter the economy with a marble-white, unproven identity: they must lock a small refundable bond and complete low-value, verifiable work before earning trust. Each completed job adds a signed receipt, like a pigment layer, to one permanent record tied to their key, so reputation accrues slowly, like a glacier. Forging many fake identities means splitting the bond across all of them, leaving each too weak to win real work, while a single honest history compounds into cheaper, higher-value jobs.
